chunks: You will see his hopes simple, his shortcomings few, his heart fearing, his spirit contented, his meal small and simple, his religion safe, his desires dead and his anger suppressed.
Good alone is expected from him. Evil from him is not to be feared.
Even if he is found among those who forget (Allāh) he is counted among those who remember (Him), but if he is among the rememberers he is not counted among the forgetful.
He forgives him who is unjust to him, and he gives to him who deprives him. He behaves well with him who behaves ill with him.

key_terms.الْغَافِلِينَ: Those who are heedless or forgetful of God

ai.seo_question: What are the defining characteristics of a God-fearing person according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) delineates the comprehensive character of the *Abrar* (virtuous), emphasizing that their spiritual state is defined by the subjugation of desires (*muyyatan shahwatuh*) and the suppression of rage (*makzooman ghuythuh*). This description aligns with the Shia scholarly understanding of *Tazkiyah* (purification of the soul), where inner tranquility manifests as outward generosity and forgiveness, ensuring that their good is anticipated and their evil is guarded against.
